facts.fact_text: The applicant is a journalist.
The applicant is a political activist.
The applicant is the chairman of a journalists' club based in Gyumri.
On 2 March 2008 at around 12.30 p.m. the applicant arrived at Theatre Square in central Gyumri.
On 2 March 2008 the applicant tried to enter Theatre Square in central Gyumri in order to hold a protest.
It is alleged that the applicant started calling on people who were present at Theatre Square to gather and to hold a demonstration.
On 2 March 2008 the applicant was refused entry to Theatre Square by police officers who were stationed there for the purpose of preventing any demonstrations from taking place.
Police officers ordered the applicant to leave Theatre Square and to stop inciting others to assemble.
The applicant was taken to a police station after disobeying the police officers' orders at Theatre Square on 2 March 2008.

The Administrative Court found that on 2 March 2008 at around 12.30 p.m. the applicant arrived at Theatre Square in Gyumri and wanted to enter the square, but was prevented and ordered to leave that area and not to call on people to gather and hold an event, which he disobeyed.

Article 43 of the Constitution of Armenia, as in force at the material time, permitted restrictions on the right to freedom of peaceful assembly under the conditions of being prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society for the protection of national security and public order, the prevention of crimes, the protection of public health and morals, or the protection of constitutional rights and freedoms, honour and good reputation of others.

Article 182 of the Code of Administrative Offences, as in force at the material time, provided that disobeying a lawful order of a military serviceman or a police officer issued in the performance of his duties of preserving public order and of ensuring public safety would result in a fine in the amount of 50 times the fixed minimum wage.
Section 38 of the Police Act (2001) provides that every citizen and public official is obliged to obey lawful orders of a police officer.

Section 38 of the Police Act (2001) provides that failure to obey lawful orders of a police officer or actions obstructing the performance of a police officer's duties result in liability in accordance with the procedure prescribed by law.
The Decree of the President of the Republic of Armenia on Declaration of a State of Emergency (No. NH-35-N) was issued on 1 March 2008.

The Decree of the President of the Republic of Armenia No. NH-35-N declared a state of emergency in Yerevan from 1 March 2008 for 20 days, in order to prevent the threat of danger to the constitutional order in the Republic of Armenia and to protect the rights and lawful interests of the population, guided by point 14 of Article 55 and point 6 of Article 117 of the Constitution of the Republic of Armenia.

The Decree of the President of the Republic of Armenia No. NH-35-N established as a temporary limitation in the area under state of emergency the banning of meetings, rallies, demonstrations, marches and other mass events.

The Decree of the President of the Republic of Armenia No. NH-35-N declared a state of emergency in Yerevan from 1 March 2008 for 20 days, in order to prevent the threat of danger to the constitutional order in the Republic of Armenia and to protect the rights and lawful interests of the population, guided by point 14 of Article 55 and point 6 of Article 117 of the Constitution of the Republic of Armenia.

Article 43 of the Constitution of Armenia, as in force at the material time, permitted restrictions on the right to freedom of peaceful assembly under the conditions of being prescribed by law and necessary in a democratic society for the protection of national security and public order, the prevention of crimes, the protection of public health and morals, or the protection of constitutional rights and freedoms, honour and good reputation of others.

The Administrative Court found, referring to the requirements of Section 10 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, that there had been no legal basis for holding a demonstration at Theatre Square in Gyumri on 2 March 2008.

Section 10 §§ 1, 2 and 4 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (2004-2011) provides that everyone has the right to hold non-mass public events without notifying the competent authority and without violating public order.
According to Section 2 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (2004-2011), 'non-mass public events' are defined as public events which have fewer than 100 participants.

Section 10 §§ 1, 2 and 4 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (2004-2011) provides that, except for cases when a non-mass public event spontaneously turns into a mass public event, mass public events may be held only after notifying the competent authority in writing.
